title: SAM-CLIP-Thermal: Leveraging large multimodal models for reliable and scalable annotation in thermal image segmentation for field plant phenotyping

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《SAM-CLIP-Thermal: Leveraging large multimodal models for reliable and scalable annotation in thermal image segmentation for field plant phenotyping》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-1】Thermal imaging enables non-invasive assessment of canopy temperature, an essential indicator of plant stress, yet the lack of color cues and strong shadow interference make plant segmentation in thermal images difficult.

evidence.text: Thermal imaging enables non-invasive assessment of canopy temperature, an essential indicator of plant stress, yet the lack of color cues and strong shadow interference make plant segmentation in thermal images difficult.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《SAM-CLIP-Thermal: Leveraging large multimodal models for reliable and scalable annotation in thermal image segmentation for field plant phenotyping》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Abstract · abstract-1-4】Building upon the SAM-CLIP framework, we design a unified pipeline spanning zero-shot inference, few-shot and low-shot fine-tuning, and active learning to maximize accuracy with minimal supervision.

【Abstract · abstract-1-7】The released datasets can be found at: https://cornell.box.com/s/dh69xf84464yrc1vlws92l1tflx7qa89.
